وما رُوي عن ابن عباس مرفوعًا: «لا صرورة في الإسلام» فهو ضعيف. رواه أبو داود (١٧٢٩)، وأحمد (٢٨٤٤، ٣١١٤)، والطحاوي في «مشكله» (١٢٨٢)، وصححه الحاكم (١/٤٤٨).

والصواب أن عمر بن عطاء في هذا الإسناد هو عمر بن عطاء بن وراز، وهو ضعيف، لا عمر بن عطاء بن أبي الخوار الثقة. وقد بيّن أحمد وابن معين الفرق بينهما، وأن رواية ابن جريج عن عمر بن عطاء عن عكرمة هي عن ابن وراز.

وقوله: «لا صرورة» قيل: الصرورة من انقطع عن النكاح وتبتل على طريقة الرهبانية، وقيل: من لم يحج قط. والحديث المرفوع لا يثبت.

The report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās as a Prophetic statement, “There is no ṣarūrah in Islam,” is weak. It was narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1729), Aḥmad (2844, 3114), al-Ṭaḥāwī in Mushkil al-Āthār (1282), and al-Ḥākim authenticated it (1/448).

The correct identification of ʿUmar ibn ʿAṭāʾ in this chain is ʿUmar ibn ʿAṭāʾ ibn Warrāz, who is weak, not the trustworthy ʿUmar ibn ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī al-Khawār. Aḥmad and Ibn Maʿīn distinguished between the two and explained that Ibn Jurayj’s narration from ʿUmar ibn ʿAṭāʾ from ʿIkrimah is from Ibn Warrāz.

The phrase “no ṣarūrah” has been explained in two ways: one who abstains from marriage and devotes himself in a monastic manner, and one who has never performed Hajj. The Prophetic report itself is not established.

قال ابن جرير الطبريّ: (( وجعلها أيضاً ميقاتاً لحجُّكم تعرفون بها وقت مناسككم وحجُّكم)». تفسيره (٢٨٣ (٣).

قال اللّه تعالى: ( الْحَجُّ أَشْهُرٌ مَعْلُومَاتٌ} [البقرة: ١٩٧].

أجمع العلماء على أنّ المراد بأشهر الحجّ ثلاثة: شوال، وذو القعدة، وذو الحجة، لكن اختلفوا هل هي ثلاثة بكم إلها، أو شهران وبعض الثالث.

فقال بعضهم: يعني بالأشهر المعلومات: شوالاً، وذا القعدة، وعشراً من ذي الحجة، هكذا ذكره البخاري عن ابن عمر معلقا عقب حديث رقم (١٥٥٩)، ونقله ابن جرير الطبري في تفسيره عن جماعة من الصحابة وغيرهم.

وقال بعضهم: بل يعني بذلك شوالا، وذا القعدة، وذا الحجة كلَّه

قال ابن عباس: “ من السنة ألا تحرم بالحج إلا في أشهر الحج “ ذكره البخاري معلقا عقب حديث رقم (١٥٥٩)، ونقله ابن جرير في تفسيره عن جماعة من التابعين أيضًا.

يعني لا يجوز نية الإحرام بالحج إلا في أشهر معلومات، بخلاف العمرة فإنها تجوز في السنة كلها.

Allah the Exalted said: “They ask you about the new moons. Say: They are markers of time for people and for Hajj.” [Surah al-Baqarah: 189]

Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: “He also made them a time marker for your pilgrimage, by which you know the timing of your rites and your Hajj.” Tafsir (3/283).

Allah the Exalted said: “Hajj is during well-known months.” [al-Baqarah: 197]

The scholars agreed that what is meant by the months of Hajj are three: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qi’dah, and Dhu al-Hijjah. But they differed over whether they are three full months, or two months and part of the third.

Some of them said that the well-known months are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qi’dah, and the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. This is how al-Bukhari mentioned it from Ibn Umar in a suspended report after hadith number (1559), and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari also reported it in his Tafsir from a group of Companions and others.

And some of them said: rather, it means Shawwal, Dhu al-Qi’dah, and all of Dhu al-Hijjah.

Ibn Abbas said: “It is from the Sunnah that one should not enter into Hajj except during the months of Hajj.” Al-Bukhari mentioned it in a suspended report after hadith number (1559), and Ibn Jarir also reported it in his Tafsir from a group of the Successors.

This means that intending consecration for Hajj is not valid except during the known months, unlike Umrah, which is allowed throughout the entire year.

It is narrated from Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, that she heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Whoever enters ihram for Hajj or ʿUmrah from al-Masjid al-Aqṣā to al-Masjid al-Ḥarām will have his past and future sins forgiven,” or, “Paradise becomes obligatory for him.”

It was narrated by Abū Dāwūd (1741), Ibn Mājah (3001, 3002), and Aḥmad (26558). The transmitters differed considerably over its text and chain. Its chain includes Yaḥyā ibn Abī Sufyān, whose status is not well established, and Ḥakīmah Umm Ḥakīm, who was declared trustworthy only by Ibn Ḥibbān; therefore the report is not established with a strong chain.

وقال تعالى: ( وَحُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ صَيْدُ الْبَرِّ مَا دُمْتُمْ حُرُمًا ) [المائدة: ٩٦].

لا خلاف بين أهل العلم في تحريم الصيد على المحرم، وفي تحريم ما صِيد من أجله، ولذا ردَّ النبيُّ ﷺ صيدَ الصعب بن جثامة الليثي؛ لأنه صاده للنبي ﷺ وأصحابه، ولم يردَّ صيدَ أبي قتادة؛ لأنه صاده لنفسه كما سيأتي.

ثم أحلَّ اللّٰه صيد البحر، وحرَّم صيد البر، وقيل: إن الحكمة في ذلك أن المسافر في البحر قد لا يجد طعامًا غير صيد البحر، بخلاف المسافر في البر فإنه يجد طعامًا، ولذا حُرِّم عليه صيد البر.

Allah the Exalted said: “O you who believe, do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram.” [Surat al-Ma’idah: 95]

And He said: “And forbidden to you is the game of the land as long as you are in a state of ihram.” [Surat al-Ma’idah: 96]

There is no disagreement among the scholars regarding the prohibition of hunting for the muhrim, and the prohibition of game hunted specifically for him. That is why the Prophet ﷺ refused the game of al-Sa‘b ibn Jaththamah al-Laythi, because he had hunted it for the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions, while he did not refuse the game of Abu Qatadah, because he hunted it for himself, as will come later.

Then Allah made sea game lawful and land game unlawful. It has been said that the wisdom in this is that a traveler at sea may not find food other than sea game, unlike the traveler on land, who can find other food. For this reason, land game was forbidden to him.

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال تعالى: ( وَأَتِمُّوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ لِلَّهِ ) [سورة البقرة: ١٩٦].

فالله تعالى يأمر بإتمام الحج والعمرة، وثبت من السنة المتواترة أن النبي ﷺ أمر بفسخ الحج إلى العمرة، فدفعًا للتعارض بين الآية وقول النبي ﷺ قالوا: هذا خاصٌّ لأصحاب النبي ﷺ، ويبقى إتمام الحج والعمرة لغيرهم إلى يوم القيامة، ويدل عليه عمل الخلفاء الراشدين غير علي بن أبي طالب، ومن بعدهم من التابعين ومن تبعهم إلى يوم الدين. وقالوا: إن السبب في ذلك أنهم كانوا في الجاهلية يعتقدون أن التمتع بالعمرة إلى الحج من أفجر الفجور، فأمرهم النبي ﷺ بفسخ الحج إلى العمرة ليبيّن جواز العمرة في أشهر الحج، وقد حصلت معرفة ذلك، فلا حاجة بعد ذلك إلى الفسخ. ولكن التمتع رخصة للمبتدئ بها توفيقًا بين أقاويل الصحابة. ولولا علمهم بأن ذلك خاصٌّ بالركب الذين كانوا مع النبي ﷺ لم يقدموا على تغيير حكم الشريعة، ولم يطاوعهم المسلمون على ذلك، ولا يجوز لمسلم أن يظن بهم ذلك. انظر: “شرح العمدة” (١/٤٩٦).

chapters.intro_en_source:
Allah Most High said: “Complete the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage for Allah.” [Surat al-Baqarah: 196]

Allah commands the completion of the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage, and it is established by widely transmitted prophetic reports that the Prophet ﷺ ordered people to change the pilgrimage into the lesser pilgrimage. To reconcile the verse with the statement of the Prophet ﷺ, some scholars said that this was specific to the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, while completing the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage remains the rule for others until the Day of Resurrection. They cited as evidence the practice of the Rightly Guided Caliphs other than ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, and those after them among the Followers and those who followed them. They also said that the reason was that in the pre-Islamic period people believed that combining the lesser pilgrimage with the pilgrimage in the pilgrimage months was one of the gravest wrongs, so the Prophet ﷺ ordered them to change the pilgrimage into the lesser pilgrimage in order to show that the lesser pilgrimage during the pilgrimage months is permissible. Once that became well known, there was no longer a need for that change. But beginning with the lesser pilgrimage and then continuing to the pilgrimage remains a concession, in order to harmonize the different statements of the Companions. Had they not known that this was specific to the group that was with the Prophet ﷺ, they would not have ventured to alter a ruling of the Sacred Law, nor would the Muslims have followed them in that. It is not permissible for a Muslim to think ill of them in that regard. See “Sharh al-‘Umdah” (1/496).

chapters.intro_en_source: It is narrated from Jabir ibn ʿAbdullah concerning a man who sees the House and raises his hands that he said: “I did not used to see anyone do this except the Jews. We performed Hajj with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he did not do it.” The report is weak. It was narrated by Abu Dawud (1870), al-Tirmidhi (855), and al-Nasaʾi (2898) through Abu Qazaʿah, from al-Muhajir al-Makki, from Jabir. Al-Muhajir al-Makki is unknown, and for that reason the scholars regarded the report as weak.

chapters.intro_en_source:
Allah Most High said: “And purify My House for those who circumambulate.” [Surat al-Hajj: 26]

And He said: “And let them circumambulate the Ancient House.” [Surat al-Hajj: 29]

The word “Ancient” here means old and ancient, as shown by His saying: “Indeed, the first House established for mankind was the one at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for all people.” [Surat Al ‘Imran: 96]

chapters.intro_en_source: It is narrated from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he combined Hajj and ʿUmrah, performed two circumambulations and two saʿys for them, then said: “This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do.” Al-Dāraquṭnī narrated it (2628, 2629). chapters.intro_en_source:
Allah Most High said: “Complete the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage for Allah. But if you are prevented, then offer whatever sacrificial animal is easy to obtain. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal reaches its place of slaughter.” [Surat al-Baqarah: 196]

Ibn Kathir said in his commentary (1/538): “His statement, ‘And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal reaches its place of slaughter,’ is connected to His statement, ‘Complete the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage for Allah,’ and is not connected to His statement, ‘But if you are prevented, then offer whatever sacrificial animal is easy to obtain,’ as Ibn Jarir claimed.”

As for the report from ʿĀʾishah that she said: I said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, shall we not build you a house or structure at Minā to shade you from the sun?” He said: “No; it is only a stopping place for whoever reaches it first,” it is weak.

It was narrated by Abū Dāwūd (2019), al-Tirmidhī (881), Ibn Mājah (3006, 3007), and al-Ḥākim (1/466–467). Its chain contains Musaykah, whose status is unknown, and Ibrāhīm ibn Muhājir, who narrated it alone and had weakness in memory; therefore it is not established.

chapters.intro_en_source: Allah the Exalted said: “Then let them complete what is required of them, fulfill their vows, and circumambulate the Ancient House.” [Surat al-Hajj: 29] This circumambulation is called the circumambulation of al-Ifadah. It is also called the circumambulation of Hajj and the circumambulation of visitation. It only takes place after standing at Arafah and spending the night at Muzdalifah. There is no disagreement about this, and the plain meaning of the Qur’an indicates it.

قال الله تعالى: ( فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ ۚ فَمَن لَّمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الْحَجِّ وَسَبْعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ ۗ تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ ۗ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن لَّمْ يَكُنْ أَهْلُهُ حَاضِرِي الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ ) [سورة البقرة: ١٩٦].

وفيه نسخ وجوب ما كان قبل الإسلام من سوق الهدي في الحج والعمرة، ولذا ساق النبي ﷺ في عمرة الحديبية، وانحصر وجوب الهدي على المتمتع والقارن، وبقي استحبابه على المفرد والمعتمر.

chapters.intro_en_source:
Allah Most High said: “Whoever enjoys the lesser pilgrimage before the greater pilgrimage must offer whatever offering is easy to obtain. But whoever cannot find one must fast three days during the pilgrimage and seven when you return. That makes ten complete. That is for the one whose family does not live near the Sacred Mosque.” [al-Baqarah: 196]

This contains the abrogation of what had been obligatory before Islam regarding bringing an offering in the pilgrimage and the lesser pilgrimage. For that reason, the Prophet ﷺ brought an offering in the Umrah of al-Hudaybiyah. The obligation of the offering then remained only upon the pilgrim doing the combined pilgrimage with a break between rites and the one combining both rites together, while it remained recommended for the pilgrim doing only the greater pilgrimage and the one doing only the lesser pilgrimage.

قال الله تعالى: ( فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ ) [سورة البقرة: ١٩٦].

عن علي بن أبي طالب، قال: ( فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ ) شاة. وعن عبد الله بن عمر، قال: ( فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ ) بدنة أو بقرة. رواه مالك في الموطأ (١٥٨، ١٦٠).

قال تعالى: ( وَالْبُدْنَ جَعَلْنَاهَا لَكُم مِّن شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ لَكُمْ فِيهَا خَيْرٌ ) [الحج: ٣٦].

عن أبي جمرة، قال: سألت ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن المتعة فأمرني بها، وسألته عن الهدي فقال: (( فيها جزور أو بقرة أو شاة أو شرك في دم )) الحديث. رواه البخاريّ (١٦٨٨).

Allah Most High said: “Whatever offering is easy to obtain.” [al-Baqarah: 196]

Ali ibn Abi Talib said regarding the verse, “whatever offering is easy to obtain”: a sheep. And Abdullah ibn Umar said: a camel or a cow. Narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta (158, 160).

Allah Most High said: “And the large sacrificial camels We have made for you among the symbols of Allah; in them there is good for you.” [al-Hajj: 36]

Abu Jamrah said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the combined pilgrimage with a break between rites, and he instructed me to do it. I asked him about the offering, and he said: “It may be a camel, a cow, a sheep, or a share in a sacrificial animal.” The rest of the hadith follows. Narrated by al-Bukhari (1688).
